subtopic: Telling the truth after a mistake
subtype: Approach: preparing the words before confessing [Thinking]
passage: Zanele rehearsed on the school bus in Durban, moving her lips. First: say it plainly, I lost your pencil box. Second: say sorry, and mean it. Third: offer to replace it from my pocket money. She practised until the words stopped shaking. At the gate she found her friend Hiroshi kicking a stone, hands in his pockets. "Hiroshi, I lost your pencil box yesterday. I am really sorry. I will buy you a new one with my pocket money." Hiroshi's face fell, then he shrugged. "It was a gift from my grandfather, but thank you for telling me." Zanele swallowed. She had not planned for that. "I will look again in the classroom too," she said.

qa.q: What three things did Zanele plan to say?
qa.a: She planned to say she lost the pencil box, say sorry and offer to replace it from her pocket money.

qa.q: What was Zanele feeling on the bus while she rehearsed?
qa.a: Nervous, since she moved her lips until the words stopped shaking. 😅

qa.q: What else could Zanele do after apologising?
qa.a: Search the classroom and the lost-property box with Hiroshi, because finding the box would mean more than a replacement.

qa.q: How might Hiroshi feel about the lost pencil box and the apology?
qa.a: Sad about the gift but appreciative of the honesty, since his face fell and then he thanked Zanele for telling him.

grounding: A girl who lost a friend's pencil box rehearses admitting it, saying sorry and offering to replace it.

subtopic: Telling the truth after a mistake
subtype: Approach: preparing the words before confessing [Thinking]
passage: Kalyani had borrowed Kiran's unicorn pencil box for the drawing period, and now it was gone. She had checked the art room, the corridor and under every desk. Kiran would be back from the sports ground in ten minutes. Kalyani sat on the bench by the school water cooler and whispered it through to herself. "First, say it straight: Kiran, I lost your pencil box. Don't say 'it got lost', that's hiding. Then sorry, properly. Then..." She had sixty rupees saved. "I'll get you a new one from my pocket money." She said it twice more under her breath. When Kiran came in, sweaty and smiling, Kalyani stood up before she could lose her nerve.

qa.q: How was Kalyani feeling on the bench?
qa.a: Nervous and guilty, afraid of losing her nerve.

qa.q: What else could Kalyani do before buying a new one?
qa.a: Ask the class teacher to check the lost-property box, in case the pencil box turns up.

qa.q: How might Kiran feel hearing it?
qa.a: Probably disappointed at first, but Kiran may value the honest words and the offer to replace it.

grounding: A girl who lost her friend's pencil box rehearses admitting it, apologising and offering to replace it from pocket money.

subtopic: Telling the truth after a mistake
subtype: Approach: preparing the words before confessing [Thinking]
passage: I'm Parul, and I share a bench with Sarita. Yesterday she lost the pencil box her friend Meenu had lent her, the one with the magnetic lid. At lunch, instead of eating, she sat with her tiffin closed, moving her lips. I heard bits: "I lost it." Then, "I'm really sorry." Then, "I'll buy you one from my pocket money." She said it over and over, like a poem for assembly. When Meenu came back from the tap, Sarita stood up and said all three, in exactly that order. Meenu looked upset for a second, then said, "Okay. Let's check the lost-property box first." I don't know how scared Sarita was, but she was twisting her tiffin strap the whole time.

qa.q: What kind of lid did the pencil box have?
What might Sarita have been feeling while rehearsing?
qa.a: Nervous and guilty, twisting her tiffin strap the whole time.

qa.q: What else could Sarita do if the box isn't in lost property?
qa.a: Keep her promise and replace it, and tell Meenu when so there's no doubt.
Meenu looked upset for a second, then calmly suggested checking the lost-property box.

grounding: A classmate watches a girl rehearse admitting she lost a friend's pencil box, apologising and offering to replace it.
